timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So compliance says protect customer data. That sounds... vague.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Exactly. The architect translates that vague requirement into specific security controls.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Encryption, access reviews, logging, retention, data loss prevention, and evidence collection.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Yes. If you cannot prove the control runs, the auditor treats it like theater.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So every rule needs an owner?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Owner, implementation, test method, evidence source, and remediation plan. That is the grown-up version.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Purview maps data and policies. Azure Policy enforces resource rules. Defender for Cloud validates posture.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So compliance is design work, not paperwork?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Exactly. Paperwork documents the design. It does not replace the design.
